paper_information.title: Identification guide for major diseases and insect-pests of wheat
paper_information.journal_or_source: Technical Bulletin no.18, ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research, Karnal
paper_information.abstract_summary: A comprehensive technical identification and management guide for major wheat diseases and insect-pests in India, covering symptoms, geographic distribution, causal organisms, and chemical/cultural control measures.
paper_information.research_objective: To provide field-level identification and management guidelines for major diseases and insect pests affecting wheat crops in India.
important_findings: Detailed identification characteristics for major rusts, smuts, bunts, and insect-pests of wheat.
Geographic zones susceptible to specific pathogens.
Recommended fungicide and insecticide treatments with specific application dosages.

general: Appears as a mass of yellow to orange urediniospores erupting from pustules arranged in long, narrow stripes on leaves, leaf sheaths, glumes and awns.
early_symptoms: Disease starts with small patches or foci of infection.
advanced_symptoms: Spreads rapidly under congenial weather in long narrow stripes between veins.
visual_field_symptoms: Orange dust comes out on fingers and clothing when touching infected leaves.
Starts in small patches or foci.

field_identification: Look for yellow to orange pustules arranged in long, narrow stripes between leaf veins.
Spores rub off as orange dust on fingers and clothing.

causes_and_risk_factors: Growing single susceptible variety over large areas
disease_development_and_spread: Spreads rapidly from initial infection foci under congenial weather.

cultural_management: Grow recently released resistant varieties recommended for the zone.
Grow yellow rust tolerant varieties and avoid use of one particular variety over large areas.
Use balanced and recommended quantity of fertilisers and avoid high dose of Nitrogen.

chemical_management.timing: Immediately on appearance of disease to avoid further spread from initial infection foci

prevention: Keep strict watch on appearance of the disease.
farmer_action_points: Inspect fields for small patches of yellow stripes on leaves.
warnings_and_limitations: Most recommended varieties for NWPZ and NHZ do not carry high level of resistance, hence chemical sprays are needed.

general: Small, circular to oval pustules with orange to light brown dusty spores on upper surface of leaves and on leaf sheaths in heavy infections.
visual_field_symptoms: Pustules mainly confined to the upper surface and irregularly distributed on leaves.

field_identification: Small, circular to oval orange to light brown dusty pustules on upper leaf surfaces.

causes_and_risk_factors: Planting a single variety over large areas

cultural_management: Grow recommended varieties for the zone.
Grow leaf rust tolerant varieties and avoid single variety over large areas.
Use balanced and recommended quantity of fertilisers and avoid high dose of nitrogen.

chemical_management.timing: Immediate spraying upon appearance of disease

prevention: Keep strict watch on appearance of the disease.
farmer_action_points: Monitor fields and apply recommended fungicides at early disease appearance.

general: Large orange-brown pustules oval or elongated in shape on stems and sometimes both sides of leaves and leaf sheaths.
advanced_symptoms: Presence of silver-colored ruptured epidermis above pustules.
Rupture of pustules releases a powdery mass of brick red colored urediniospores.
visual_field_symptoms: Oval or elongated orange-brown pustules on stems with silver ruptured epidermis.

field_identification: Large, oval or elongated orange-brown pustules on stems with ruptured silvery epidermis releasing brick-red powdery spores.

causes_and_risk_factors: Growing single variety over large areas

cultural_management: Grow recommended varieties for the zone.
Grow stem rust tolerant varieties and avoid single variety over large areas.
Use balanced and recommended quantity of fertilisers and avoid high dose of nitrogen.

chemical_management.timing: Immediate spraying of affected areas upon appearance

prevention: Keep strict watch on appearance of the disease.
farmer_action_points: Check stems for elongated pustules and apply propiconazole @ 0.1% immediately.

general: Extremely difficult to diagnose in the field because few kernels in an ear head get infected.
Grains are either partially affected or in severe cases whole grain is converted into black powder of bunt spores.
visual_field_symptoms: Normally noticed after threshing where grains show black powdery mass.

field_identification: Difficult to identify in field; detected after threshing by partial or complete conversion of kernels into black powder.

causes_and_risk_factors: Frequent rains during ear head emergence.

favorable_conditions.rainfall: Frequent rains during ear head emergence

cultural_management: Use certified or disease-free seed.
Follow crop rotation and avoid growing wheat for 2-3 years in highly infected fields.
Zero tillage helps in reducing Karnal bunt incidence.

chemical_management.timing: At the time of 50% flowering; repeat after 15 days if it rains

prevention: Use certified or disease free seed.
farmer_action_points: Inspect threshed grain for black powdery kernels.
Spray propiconazole @ 0.1% at 50% flowering in prone areas.

general: Small, dark brown lesions 1 to 2 mm long without chlorotic margin.
Lesions extend very quickly into oval to elongated blotches, light brown to dark brown, coalescing and causing death of the leaf.
early_symptoms: Small, dark brown lesions 1 to 2 mm long without chlorotic margin.
advanced_symptoms: Oval to elongated blotches that coalesce leading to leaf death.
Shrivelled grain and black point (dark staining of embryo end of seed) if spikelets are affected.
visual_field_symptoms: Dark brown small lesions extending into larger blotches causing leaf death.

field_identification: Look for small dark brown lesions without chlorotic margins expanding into blighted blotches on leaves.

cultural_management: Cultivation of recommended resistant varieties.

prevention: Use seed treatment with carboxin or carboxin+thiram.
farmer_action_points: Spray difenoconazole or triadimefon upon initial symptom appearance.

general: Superficial greyish small patches of white cottony growth on leaves, sheath, stem, and even on ear head.
early_symptoms: Superficial greyish small patches of white cottony growth.
advanced_symptoms: White cottony growth covers the whole leaf and other aerial parts.
White patches turn brownish to dull tan color late in the season due to formation of cleistothecia.
visual_field_symptoms: White cottony fungal patches on leaves and stems turning brownish later.

field_identification: White cottony or greyish patches on leaves, sheaths, and stems.

cultural_management: Use recommended quantity of seed to avoid excessively dense stands.

chemical_management.timing: At appearance of disease in disease prone areas

prevention: Avoid excessively dense stands by using recommended seed rates.
farmer_action_points: Look for white cottony patches on foliage and apply triadimefon 25% WP @ 0.1%.

general: Spore mass covered with a delicate silvery membrane of host origin which usually ruptures before complete emergence of ears, exposing dark olive-brown powdery mass of spores.
early_symptoms: Smutted spike emerges from boot leaf a few days earlier than healthy plants.
advanced_symptoms: Normal spikelets replaced entirely by dark olive-brown powdery mass of spores.
visual_field_symptoms: Black/dark brown powdery heads emerging earlier than healthy ears.

field_identification: Ears replaced by dark olive-brown powdery spore masses emerging earlier than healthy plants.

cultural_management: Use disease free seed.
Rouge out and destroy infected tillers.

farmer_action_points: Rouge out infected tillers in the field.
Treat seeds with carboxin, carbendazim, or tebuconazole before planting.

general: Black narrow elongated blisters appear on leaves between veins; ruptured blisters expose black spore balls and split leaves into ribbons.
Black streaks on stunted stems with dwarfed internodes.
advanced_symptoms: Infected plants stunted and spindly with more tillers (grass-like appearance).
Inflorescence stunted, distorted, frequently sterile, bearing black streaks.
Spike development stops before head emerges from leaf whorl (no seeds produced).
visual_field_symptoms: Black narrow blisters on leaves splitting into ribbons, stunted plants with grass-like appearance.

field_identification: Black narrow blisters on leaves splitting into ribbons and black streaks on stems of stunted, tillering plants.

cultural_management: Use disease free seed.

prevention: Use disease free seed and treat seed before planting.
farmer_action_points: Inspect sandy soil fields for stunted plants with black leaf streaks.
Apply seed treatments using carboxin or tebuconazole.

early_symptoms: Water soaked spots with deep green color on leaves turning into brown boat-shaped necrotic spots.
advanced_symptoms: Glumes show elliptical lesions with reddish brown to dark grey margins and white to light brown center.
Ears rendered shrunken, shrivelled and deformed with no grain filling.
visual_field_symptoms: Boat-shaped brown necrotic spots on leaves and bleached/deformed spikes.

field_identification: Brown boat-shaped spots on leaves and bleached, shrunken spikes.

causes_and_risk_factors: Grassy weeds acting as secondary hosts (Eleusine indica, Leersia, Echinochloa, Brachiaria, Digitaria, Lolium, Cenchrus, Chloris)
disease_development_and_spread: Grassy weeds act as secondary hosts and spread the disease in wheat.
severity_and_yield_loss: Heavy yield loss or total crop failure

cultural_management: Use certified and disease free seed.
Use resistant wheat varieties.
Regularly remove and destroy weeds and grasses in and around the wheat field.

farmer_action_points: Clear grassy weeds from field borders.
warnings_and_limitations: Till date the disease is not reported from India (noted as present in Bangladesh and South America).

diseases.disease_name: Fusarium head blight or head scab

general: Small, water soaked spots at base or middle of glumes, rachis or first floret spreading within the earhead.
early_symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on glumes, rachis, or florets.
advanced_symptoms: Premature whitening or bleaching of ear head.
White, pinky-salmon mass of spores on infected glumes and spikelets under warm and moist conditions.
Developing grain turns shrunken, shrivelled, rough surfaced, discoloured soft-gray, chalky white to light-brown ('tombstones').
visual_field_symptoms: Premature bleaching of ear heads and pinkish-salmon spore masses.

field_identification: Bleached ear heads with possible pinkish spore masses and shrunken chalky kernels ('tombstones').

cultural_management: Use certified and disease free seed.
Use resistant wheat varieties.

prevention: Use certified and disease-free seeds and resistant varieties.
farmer_action_points: Inspect fields for bleached heads and treat seeds before planting.

diseases.disease_name: Hill Bunt or Stinking Smut or Common bunt

general: Bunted heads are slender, bluish-green and stay greener longer than healthy heads.
Bunt balls change to dull gray-brown at maturity.
Grains full of black powder giving a foul smell resembling rotten fish.
advanced_symptoms: Fragile covering of bunt balls ruptures at harvest, producing clouds of spores.
visual_field_symptoms: Foul smell resembling rotten fish in the field, bluish-green slender heads.

field_identification: Identified by a distinct foul smell of rotten fish in the field and bluish-green slender heads with gray-brown bunt balls.

disease_development_and_spread: Spores released in clouds when bunt balls rupture at harvest.

cultural_management: Use certified and disease free seed.
Sowing of disease resistant varieties.

prevention: Use certified seed and seed treatments.
farmer_action_points: Check for rotten-fish odor in fields and treat seeds with carboxin or carbendazim.

general: Pericarps of maturing wheat kernels turn dark brown to black with discoloration restricted to the germ end of kernel.
visual_field_symptoms: Dark brown to black discoloration at the germ end of harvested kernels.

field_identification: Dark brown to black discoloration at the germ end of kernels.

cultural_management: Use certified and disease free seed.
Sowing of disease resistant varieties.

prevention: Use certified and disease free seed and treat seeds.
farmer_action_points: Inspect harvested grains for black germ ends.

paper_level_notes: The document also covers major insect-pests of wheat including Foliar Aphids, Termites, Root aphid, Pink Stem Borer, Brown wheat mite, Army worm, and Shoot fly on pages 28-41.
